subject: multistate dynamic occupancy - troubleshooting model initiation

messages.author: bed9858844040a0b
messages.subject: multistate dynamic occupancy - troubleshooting model initiation
parts:
Hi all. I am having trouble with a couple issues trying to initiate the attached model. Would greatly appreciate any assistance helping me see what I'm doing wrong. In addition to the model code, I've attached the R objects that I'm feeding to nimble. Once these files are located in the designated workspace, running the following should replicate what I am seeing:

source("MultiStateOcc_dynamic_habitat.nimble")
params <- R.utils::loadObject("params")
inits <- R.utils::loadObject("inits")
constants.inp <- R.utils::loadObject(" constants.inp  ")
data.inp <- R.utils::loadObject("data.inp")
model <- nimbleModel(code = model, name = "model", constants = constants.inp,
                       data = data.inp, inits = inits)

Issues:
1. In the course of initialization, I get "Error in inprod(model$beta.psi[1:2] * model$X.hab[getNodeFunctionIndexedInfo(INDEXEDNODEINFO_, :
argument "v2" is missing, with no default". Am I erring in how I am using 'inprod'? The model code line referenced in the error is line 30, but I'm also not getting phi or rho to initialize (lines 41-44). I am providing values for beta.psi and X.hab. After running the initialization, `model$beta.psi` returns '0  0' and `sum(is.na(model$X.hab))` returns '0'.
2. The second and (apparently) independent issue is that I am not getting 'z.pair' to initialize (line 61). I tried specifying this node first with 'z.pair[j] <- (z[site.ind[j], year.ind[j]] == 3)' and now as 'z.pair[j] <- step(z[site.ind[j], year.ind[j]] - 2.5)'. Neither appears to work even though I am providing initial values for 'z'.

One thing I am wondering is if my constants are not getting sent to the model properly. I can't seem to see any of the constants I've provided in the model object (e.g., 'model$k.hab' and 'model$nsurveys' don't return anything), although I don't remember trying to look for these specifically in the past, i.e., not sure if constants are held in the model in the same way that data objects and variables are.

messages.author: bed9858844040a0b
messages.subject: Re: multistate dynamic occupancy - troubleshooting model initiation
parts:
I was able to get the attached version of my model to properly initialize. It appears the 'inprod' function is not operating as intended or as it has before. I think I've got it to work fine before, but for this model, I needed to bypass 'inprod' by writing out each of the terms in my regression models to get this to work. 

Unless I'm making some error, it appears there may be a bug with 'inprod'?

messages.author: d78486bfff620d81
messages.subject: Re: multistate dynamic occupancy - troubleshooting model initiation
parts:
Hi Quresh,

You need `inprod(x[1:3], y[1:3])` not `inprod(x[1:3] * y[1:3])`.

Easy to overlook the subtle syntax error, though the error message does indicate what is going on: 'argument "v2" is missing, with no default'.

-Chris
